messages:
ashley: Heads-up — after rolling kernel + NVIDIA driver 535.56 onto us-west1-gpu-pool-1 we saw multiple nodes re-register with different MIG UUIDs. Kubernetes device-plugin no longer matches profiles, several pods stuck Pending.

sam: Which pool and how many nodes affected?

ashley: us-west1-gpu-pool-1, ~12 nodes so far. Scheduler logs show repeated: "no matching device plugin entry for mig-uuid=GPU-..." and kubelet reports reduced capacity.

jorge: Can you paste output of `nvidia-smi -L` and `kubectl describe node` for one affected node?

ashley: quick snippets:
```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-abc123...)
No MIG devices found
```
And scheduler: `FailedScheduling 0/24 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb.`

infra-bot: Detected 12 nodes with MIG device mapping changes in cluster us-west1 (auto-ticket INF-4231 created).

mira: Did the nodes reboot during the driver update? New driver releases sometimes normalize per-MIG UUIDs which breaks device-plugin state.

kevin: Confirmed something similar in the driver 535.x notes: there's a change to NVML _and_ MIG instance ordering when combined with kernel patches. Could be UUIDs regenerated on re-init.

sam: Quick mitigation: restart the nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet on a single node to force re-registration and see if kubelet picks up new capacity.

ashley: I tried restarting the plugin on one node — plugin re-created MIG entries, but scheduler still had old cached allocations for that node. Some pods stayed pending until node was drained and re-registered.

jorge: Proposed controlled remediation: cordon+drain affected nodes, restart device-plugin, ensure `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows updated allocatable resources, then uncordon. Do canary 2 nodes first.

mira: Rollback option: revert to previous driver (535.54) — but that requires a node reboot and has its own risk in prod. Prefer node-level cordon/drain if possible.

kevin: Also check for kernel module order / DKMS race: if nvidia kernel module loaded before the NVML init the MIG devices might be enumerated differently. If we re-load modules in the right order it may keep UUIDs stable.

ashley: I put a short runbook in the ticket with commands:
```
# example remediation steps
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
ssh root@<node> "systemctl restart nvidia-device-plugin && sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia"
# verify
nvidia-smi -L
kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME,ALLOCATABLE
```

sam: Let's schedule a canary tonight for 2 nodes in staging, then roll to the 12 affected in waves. Keep SLA teams in the loop.

infra-bot: Maintenance job scheduled: canary cordon/drain 2 nodes at 1802469400.

mira: Noted cost impact — several GPU workloads temporarily shifted to dedicated capacity and bumped hourly spend. Logging cost alert to FIN-ops.

ashley: Action items: (1) canary tonight, (2) if canary stable, wave drains + plugin restarts, (3) fallback plan: driver rollback and full node reboot. Monitoring: watch Pending pods and NGX/driver logs. Please update INF-4231 with any changes. :warning:
